title: The Hidden Window That Shapes Every Leader's Success
author: By Title Only
summary: By Title Only uses the Overton Window concept to explain why leaders struggle with feedback. Every person has a limited range of truths they can emotionally accept at any moment. Feedback outside that window feels like attack, not insight. Great leadership isn't forcing truths down people's throats but expanding windows so they're ready to hear. Leaders impact both their team's windows (by creating psychological safety) and their own (by seeking feedback on biases and habits). Widening your window unlocks possibilities and creates new versions of yourself who leads, listens, and lives better.
points: Every person has a limited window of truths they can emotionally process.
Feedback outside the window feels like attack even when accurate.
Leaders must expand the team's windows by creating psychological safety.
Great leadership widens windows so people become ready to hear truth.
Your own window expansion unlocks possibilities you never knew existed.
quotes: Every person has a limited range of truths they are capable of accepting at any given moment.
Open the window too much and you freeze. Open it too little and you will evaporate.
The range of acceptable ideas can and will change throughout time. Great leadership is not forcing truths down throats but widening windows so they hear it.
When you widen your window you create new versions of yourself that lead and live better.” Archived from The Best Leadership Newsletter on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
